in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. I'm asking about my son Alex, who's 18 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'd like to learn more about Alex's situation.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any approved education right now. He's finished school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need to understand Alex's current situation a bit more.

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask another important question:

**Is Alex currently claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? If so, when did he register and when did he leave education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all the information I needed. Based on your circumstances, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Since Alex is 18 years old (over 16), Child Benefit can only continue if he is under 20 **and** stays in approved education or training. As Alex is not currently in approved education or training, you do not qualify for Child Benefit for him.

There is also a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, this doesn't apply to Alex because he is 18 (not 16 or 17) and has not registered with these services.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he starts approved education or training - you may become eligible again, so it would be worth reconsidering at that point.
